title: Authorize the addressed project
brief: User Alice owns project A and submits an update URL containing Bob's project B.
explanation: Authentication establishes identity but does not authorize access to an arbitrary entity ID.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: User Alice owns project A and submits an update URL containing Bob's project B. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Load or mutate the project through an ownership-aware operation.
Send the request directly without using the filtered UI. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Alice can update A through the normal route.
B remains unchanged and its private fields are not disclosed.
Recovery evidence: Change only the route ID while retaining Alice's valid session. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Change only the route ID while retaining Alice's valid session.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does every operation use the authenticated identity rather than a body-supplied owner?
stretch: Add the same authorization matrix for reads, archives, restores, and exports.

title: Ignore forged ownership fields
brief: An authenticated create request includes ownerId set to another user's ID.
explanation: Ownership derives from trusted session context rather than client-authored fields.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An authenticated create request includes ownerId set to another user's ID. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Remove owner identity from the writable input contract.
Submit valid project data with conflicting owner fields. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The saved owner is the authenticated user.
No request can create or transfer ownership by adding an extra property.
Recovery evidence: Repeat through an older API client that sends whole entity objects. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Repeat through an older API client that sends whole entity objects.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does schema stripping hide an attempted privileged write without clear policy?
stretch: Add explicit rejection for reserved fields and safe audit categorization.

title: Expire sessions during editing
brief: Open a project editor, expire the session, then submit a long drafted goal.
explanation: An expired session blocks mutation while preserving recoverable local work.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Open a project editor, expire the session, then submit a long drafted goal. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Map authentication failure separately from validation and storage failures.
Save after expiry, sign in again, and retry deliberately. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: No unauthenticated write reaches storage.
The draft survives the expired-session response.
Recovery evidence: Change the project remotely before the user signs in again. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Change the project remotely before the user signs in again.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does reauthentication also require fresh revision validation?
stretch: Show a comparison before retrying a draft after a long authentication gap.

title: Authorize nested resources
brief: Alice requests comment C-7 through project A although C-7 belongs to project B.
explanation: A nested route must verify the relationship between every addressed resource.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Alice requests comment C-7 through project A although C-7 belongs to project B. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Constrain comment lookup by both comment ID and authorized project ID.
Try valid, mismatched, and nonexistent project-comment pairs. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Valid authorized pairs return the intended comment.
A mismatched pair never exposes another project's comment.
Recovery evidence: Reuse the comment ID with a forged request-body project ID. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Reuse the comment ID with a forged request-body project ID.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the query enforce the relationship instead of trusting route structure?
stretch: Apply the same rule to attachments, evidence, and membership endpoints.

title: Prevent client-chosen roles
brief: A viewer submits a project-edit request with role set to owner in its JSON body.
explanation: Role decisions must come from current authoritative membership records.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A viewer submits a project-edit request with role set to owner in its JSON body. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Decode writable project fields separately from authorization context.
Send the forged role with a valid viewer session. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Permitted viewer reads continue working.
The write is denied and the stored membership stays unchanged.
Recovery evidence: Modify a local browser cache to display an editor button. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Modify a local browser cache to display an editor button.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the service independently authorize the command after UI gating?
stretch: Add contract tests for every reserved authorization field.

title: Choose nondisclosing missing responses
brief: An outsider probes one real private project ID and one nonexistent ID.
explanation: Access failures should not reveal private existence unless the product intentionally permits it.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An outsider probes one real private project ID and one nonexistent ID. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define a consistent external response policy while retaining safe internal diagnostics.
Compare status, body shape, and visible messages for both probes. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The caller receives the documented nondisclosing result.
Private names and owner details never enter error payloads.
Recovery evidence: Trigger a storage failure during the authorization lookup. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Trigger a storage failure during the authorization lookup.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does error mapping preserve operational failures without exposing entity content?
stretch: Review timing and enumeration limits as separate concerns from response wording.

title: Apply authorization to exports
brief: A viewer can open a summary but requests a full project export containing private notes.
explanation: Export is an independent data-access operation with its own allowed field scope.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A viewer can open a summary but requests a full project export containing private notes. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Authorize the export and select fields according to the requesting role.
Compare exports produced by owner, editor, viewer, and outsider. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Each artifact contains only the fields allowed for its role.
Hidden notes cannot leak through a download route.
Recovery evidence: Revoke access while the export job is preparing its snapshot. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Revoke access while the export job is preparing its snapshot.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does artifact download recheck access when completion occurs later?
stretch: Use expiring download grants tied to the authorized artifact and principal.

title: Recheck access at mutation time
brief: An editor loads a project, then loses membership before submitting an update.
explanation: Previously granted UI access does not authorize later mutation indefinitely.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An editor loads a project, then loses membership before submitting an update. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Check current membership inside the write operation's consistency boundary.
Pause submission, revoke membership, then continue the command. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The command follows the current access policy.
A stale open tab cannot retain editing privileges through cached role data.
Recovery evidence: Restore membership and retry with a refreshed project revision. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Restore membership and retry with a refreshed project revision.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Are role and entity revision assumptions revalidated together?
stretch: Document how long-running jobs respond to permission changes.

title: Separate authorization from validation
brief: An outsider submits malformed input to a private project's update endpoint.
explanation: Validation errors should not disclose private record details before access is established.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An outsider submits malformed input to a private project's update endpoint. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define which envelope checks precede authorization and which domain checks follow it.
Compare malformed requests from an owner and outsider. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Authorized users receive useful field-level errors.
Outsiders learn no stored values through validation comparisons.
Recovery evidence: Cause a uniqueness check to reference another private project name. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Cause a uniqueness check to reference another private project name.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does a convenient shared validator query protected data too early?
stretch: Add a test asserting repository call order for unauthorized requests.

title: Protect the last owner
brief: A project has one owner who attempts to remove their own membership.
explanation: Every active shared project needs the ownership structure promised by its product rules.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A project has one owner who attempts to remove their own membership. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Validate remaining owners atomically before role reduction or removal.
Attempt removal, demotion, and transfer with one owner. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: A valid transfer leaves an authorized owner afterward.
The project never becomes ownerless through self-removal.
Recovery evidence: Race two owners each removing their own ownership. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Race two owners each removing their own ownership.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the invariant survive concurrent membership changes?
stretch: Provide an explicit project-closure flow for intentional ownership termination.

title: Prevent role escalation by editors
brief: An editor invites a collaborator while requesting an owner role.
explanation: Membership administration permissions are distinct from ordinary content editing.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An editor invites a collaborator while requesting an owner role. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define a capability matrix and enforce allowed target roles server-side.
Exercise each actor role against each requested membership role. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Only documented administrator capabilities succeed.
Editors cannot gain ownership indirectly through invitation or role update.
Recovery evidence: Change the request method or endpoint while keeping the same intent. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Change the request method or endpoint while keeping the same intent.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does every membership mutation share the same policy service?
stretch: Generate role-matrix tests from a declarative policy table.

title: Paginate comments with stable cursors
brief: Several comments share a timestamp and new comments arrive between page requests.
explanation: A cursor needs a total order and stable boundary semantics.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Several comments share a timestamp and new comments arrive between page requests. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Order by timestamp plus unique ID and encode both in the cursor.
Fetch pages while inserting comments around the boundary. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Existing comments appear once in the defined traversal.
Tied timestamps never cause skipped or duplicated comments.
Recovery evidence: Delete the comment that supplied the previous page's cursor. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Delete the comment that supplied the previous page's cursor.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the cursor depend on a row still existing?
stretch: Add cursor versioning before changing the ordering contract.

title: Authorize comment edits by policy
brief: An editor tries to modify another member's comment on an editable project.
explanation: Project edit rights do not automatically define authorship-edit rights.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An editor tries to modify another member's comment on an editable project. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Specify author, moderator, and owner capabilities for comment mutation.
Test same-author, other-author, removed-member, and moderator cases. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Allowed edits retain original author identity and creation time.
Unauthorized edits leave content and revision unchanged.
Recovery evidence: Remove the original author after a comment is published. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Remove the original author after a comment is published.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does historical authorship remain meaningful when membership changes?
stretch: Add a moderator correction event instead of impersonating the original author.

title: Handle removed members in history
brief: Remove a member who authored twenty comments and several project edits.
explanation: Removing access must not erase or reassign historical authorship unintentionally.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Remove a member who authored twenty comments and several project edits. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Separate membership lifecycle from immutable event actor references.
Remove the member and inspect old comments and audit entries. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: History remains attributable using the declared display policy.
Removal never transfers old comments to the current owner.
Recovery evidence: Change the removed user's display name later. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Change the removed user's display name later.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does history use a current profile or a recorded actor snapshot intentionally?
stretch: Support anonymization through an explicit policy with retained event integrity.

title: Filter comments before pagination
brief: A project contains private moderator comments interleaved with public member comments.
explanation: Visibility filtering must happen before page boundaries and counts are calculated.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A project contains private moderator comments interleaved with public member comments. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Apply role-aware filtering in the authoritative query.
Fetch consecutive pages as viewer and moderator. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Viewer pages contain only permitted comments with coherent cursors.
Page totals and gaps do not expose hidden comment content.
Recovery evidence: Insert a hidden comment at the current cursor boundary. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Insert a hidden comment at the current cursor boundary.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does post-fetch filtering produce short pages or information leaks?
stretch: Avoid total counts when exact private-inclusive counts would disclose hidden activity.

title: Validate membership changes against self-lockout
brief: An owner transfers ownership and immediately loses access under the selected policy.
explanation: A legitimate access change should clearly describe its consequence before execution.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An owner transfers ownership and immediately loses access under the selected policy. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Show resulting roles and enforce the same transition server-side.
Transfer ownership and inspect both users' subsequent capabilities. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The final role set matches the confirmed transition.
The original owner is not shown controls they can no longer use.
Recovery evidence: Lose the response after the transfer commits. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Lose the response after the transfer commits.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Can the original owner discover the resulting state without repeating the transfer?
stretch: Add an operation receipt visible to both affected principals where policy permits.

title: Make comments text-safe
brief: Post a comment containing HTML, Markdown links, and an image-like payload.
explanation: Comment formatting must preserve text safety across list, detail, and notification views.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Post a comment containing HTML, Markdown links, and an image-like payload. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Choose plain text or a restricted renderer with explicit allowed constructs.
Render the same payload in every comment surface. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Allowed formatting appears consistently and safely.
No script, credential-bearing link, or unexpected remote image executes.
Recovery evidence: Edit a safe comment into the hostile fixture. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Edit a safe comment into the hostile fixture.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does sanitization run on every rendering path rather than only creation?
stretch: Add a preview that uses exactly the production rendering pipeline.

title: Review list-query tenant scope
brief: An agent optimizes member listing by fetching memberships only by user ID.
explanation: Performance refactoring must preserve project scope and visibility constraints.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An agent optimizes member listing by fetching memberships only by user ID. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Trace query predicates back to authenticated principal and addressed project.
Seed two projects sharing one user and compare member-list responses. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Each list contains only the addressed project's permitted memberships.
Cross-project roles cannot influence the displayed capabilities.
Recovery evidence: Swap project IDs while reusing a cached response key. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Swap project IDs while reusing a cached response key.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does caching include every authorization-relevant dimension?
stretch: Add a query contract test that asserts both result rows and tenant isolation.

title: Return a useful conflict snapshot
brief: Two editors change the same project goal from revision twelve.
explanation: A conflict response should support recovery without discarding the losing draft.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Two editors change the same project goal from revision twelve. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Return the current authorized revision and preserve submitted field values.
Commit one edit, then submit the other against revision twelve. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The loser can compare draft and current content.
The stale command never overwrites the accepted edit.
Recovery evidence: Revoke access before building the conflict response. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Revoke access before building the conflict response.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does conflict detail obey the same read authorization as ordinary detail views?
stretch: Offer field-level merge only when its assumptions are visible.

title: Keep revision checks atomic
brief: A service reads revision five, compares it in application code, then updates later.
explanation: A separate read and write leaves a race between validation and mutation.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A service reads revision five, compares it in application code, then updates later. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Use a conditional update whose predicate includes expected revision.
Synchronize two writes after both initial reads. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Only one conflicting update succeeds.
Both cannot return success with the same resulting revision.
Recovery evidence: Add a delay immediately before the database mutation. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Add a delay immediately before the database mutation.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does affected-row count map to conflict without a second unsafe guess?
stretch: Distinguish missing and conflicting rows through an authorized follow-up read.

title: Avoid whole-object conflict merges
brief: One editor changes the title while another changes the description from the same snapshot.
explanation: A merge strategy must state which independent fields can be combined safely.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: One editor changes the title while another changes the description from the same snapshot. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Track base values and explicit edited fields instead of spreading full snapshots.
Attempt the merge with independent and overlapping field changes. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Independent changes combine only under the documented policy.
Overlapping edits require a visible decision.
Recovery evidence: Change a hidden server-managed field during the merge. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Change a hidden server-managed field during the merge.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the merge preserve fields neither editor owns?
stretch: Add a property-level conflict report linked to source revisions.

title: Handle archived conflicts
brief: An owner archives a project while an editor saves a stale active snapshot.
explanation: Lifecycle transitions must not be undone by unrelated stale content updates.

experiment: Restore the project and retry with its current revision.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does revision conflict handling accidentally resubmit an old whole entity?
stretch: Offer an explicit restore-and-apply flow with a fresh confirmation.

explanation: Deployment order must allow old and new writers during the transition window.

Exercise old and new clients against each rollout stage. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

experiment: Pause backfill halfway and deploy the new reader.

title: Backfill without overwriting edits

explanation: Backfill should modify only rows still matching its original missing-value condition.

title: Validate conflict retries

title: Test old clients after new writes

explanation: Old writers must not erase unfamiliar fields when editing familiar ones.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A new client writes category metadata that an old client cannot display. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.

checks: The category metadata survives the old-client edit.

title: Hash invitation secrets

explanation: A database leak should not expose directly usable invitation tokens.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Create an invitation link whose bearer token grants access to project Alpha. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.

title: Enforce expiry at acceptance

Check expiry using trusted time inside the acceptance operation.

Release two acceptance commands through a test barrier. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Exactly one allowed redemption transition occurs.

title: Bind invitations to intended identity

Compare the trusted account identity with the invitation's recipient policy.

title: Recheck inviter authority
brief: An owner creates an invitation, then loses ownership before it is accepted.

title: Handle existing membership
brief: Accept an editor invitation while already holding viewer membership in the same project.
explanation: Acceptance needs an explicit role-combination policy instead of duplicate rows.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Accept an editor invitation while already holding viewer membership in the same project. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
